hypotheses: Salermide is a sirtuin inhibitor; its histone response may resemble that of other epigenetic modulators such as methylstat (histone demethylase inhibitor) or zebularine/decitabine (DNMT inhibitors), which show high anchor similarity.

The strong H3K79me0/me1 signal in the anchor suggests a loss of H3K79 methylation; EPZ-5676 (DOT1L inhibitor) directly reduces H3K79 methylation and may serve as a mechanistic donor despite lower anchor similarity.
UNC1215 (L3MBTL3 antagonist) affects chromatin reader domains and may produce histone mark changes similar to salermide, given moderate anchor similarity.
object.evidence_gap: No direct ChIP-seq or histone modification data for salermide in A375 at 10 uM/24h; donor responses are from different cell lines and assays, and anchor similarity does not guarantee transferable histone perturbation.
